summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to reinstate tax-exempt advance refunding bonds by repealing the general prohibition and instead permitting them for private activity bonds and other bonds subject to limits on the number of refundings, mandatory redemption timelines, temporary investment periods, and debt service savings requirements.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the tax code to reinstate advance refunding of certain bonds. It does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any federal spending programs or outlays. Any fiscal effects are indirect through tax revenue changes rather than direct spending.

The core purpose is to amend IRC Section 149(d) to restore the ability to issue tax-exempt advance refunding bonds under defined conditions, reversing restrictions from the 2017 TCJA. This expands a tax expenditure by permitting more tax-exempt municipal and private-activity bond issuances, which reduces federal tax revenue and provides a tax advantage to bond issuers and holders.

The bill would reduce federal tax revenue by expanding tax-exempt bond authority, which could modestly increase deficits. However, the legislation does not contain any debt-ceiling, deficit-reduction, or fiscal-rule provisions, so the connection is incidental.
